claim: opencode has exactly two kinds of agent: primary agents and subagents.
quote: There are two types of agents in OpenCode; primary agents and subagents.

claim: Primary agents are the ones you talk to directly, and you switch between them with Tab or the switch_agent keybind.
quote: Primary agents are the main assistants you interact with directly. You can cycle through them using the **Tab** key, or your configured `switch_agent` keybind.

claim: Two primary agents ship built in: Build and Plan.
quote: OpenCode comes with two built-in primary agents, **Build** and **Plan**.

claim: Subagents are invoked by primary agents for specific tasks, or manually by @ mentioning them.
quote: Subagents are specialized assistants that primary agents can invoke for specific tasks. You can also manually invoke them by **@ mentioning** them in your messages.

claim: Three subagents ship built in: General, Explore, and Scout.
quote: OpenCode comes with three built-in subagents, **General**, **Explore**, and **Scout**.

claim: Build is the default primary agent and has every tool enabled.
quote: Build is the **default** primary agent with all tools enabled. This is the standard agent for development work where you need full access to file operations and system commands.

claim: Plan is a restricted agent for analysis, using permissions to prevent unintended changes.
quote: A restricted agent designed for planning and analysis. We use a permission system to give you more control and prevent unintended changes.

claim: Under Plan, file edits and bash commands default to ask.
quote: By default, all of the following are set to `ask`:

claim: General is a full-access subagent for multi-step work, useful for parallel units of work.
quote: A general-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks. Has full tool access (except todo), so it can make file changes when needed.

claim: Explore is fast and read-only, and cannot modify files.
quote: A fast, read-only agent for exploring codebases. Cannot modify files.

claim: Scout is read-only and aimed at external docs and dependency research.
quote: A read-only agent for external docs and dependency research.

claim: Tab cycles primary agents during a session.
quote: For primary agents, use the **Tab** key to cycle through them during a session.

claim: You can customize built-in agents or write your own, in two configuration formats.
quote: You can customize the built-in agents or create your own through configuration. Agents can be configured in two ways:

quote: You can also define agents using markdown files. Place them in:

claim: A markdown agent's filename becomes its name.
quote: The markdown file name becomes the agent name. For example, `review.md` creates a `review` agent.

claim: The model key overrides which model an agent uses, letting you match model to task.
quote: Use the `model` config to override the model for this agent. Useful for using different models optimized for different tasks.

claim: Model IDs use a provider/model-id format.
quote: The model ID in your OpenCode config uses the format `provider/model-id`.

claim: The prompt key points at a custom system prompt file for the agent.
quote: Specify a custom system prompt file for this agent with the `prompt` config. The prompt file should contain instructions specific to the agent's purpose.

claim: Prompt file paths resolve relative to the config file, so they work globally and per project.
quote: This path is relative to where the config file is located. So this works for both the global OpenCode config and the project specific config.

claim: Each permission key takes ask, allow, or deny.
quote: You can configure permissions to manage what actions an agent can take. Each permission key can be set to:

claim: Global permissions can be overridden per agent.
quote: You can override these permissions per agent.

claim: The last matching permission rule wins, so wildcards go first and specific rules after.
quote: Since the last matching rule takes precedence, put the `*` wildcard first and specific rules after.

claim: The steps key caps how many agentic iterations an agent runs before it must answer in text.
quote: Control the maximum number of agentic iterations an agent can perform before being forced to respond with text only.

claim: With no steps limit, an agent iterates until the model stops or you interrupt.
quote: If this is not set, the agent will continue to iterate until the model chooses to stop or the user interrupts the session.

claim: maxSteps is deprecated in favour of steps.
quote: The legacy `maxSteps` field is deprecated. Use `steps` instead.

claim: A JSON agent block nests each agent under an agent key, with its settings inside.
A markdown agent uses YAML frontmatter for description, mode, model, temperature and permission, with the body as the system prompt.
quote:
---
description: Reviews code for quality and best practices
mode: subagent
model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514
temperature: 0.1
permission:
  edit: deny
  bash: deny
---

You are in code review mode. Focus on:

- Code quality and best practices
- Potential bugs and edge cases
- Performance implications
- Security considerations

Provide constructive feedback without making direct changes.
